# FilCam — Manual & RAW DNG Camera App for Android

> Manual camera for Android: ISO, shutter, Kelvin white balance, manual focus, free RAW DNG, 43 film looks, focus peaking and a histogram. No account; Pro has no ads.

Source: https://trunghieuvn.github.io/filmode-camera/

Manual camera & RAW DNG for Android

# Every dial a *DSLR* has. In the phone you already carry.

FilCam puts ISO, shutter, exposure compensation, white balance in Kelvin and manual focus distance on real rulers, with **P, S, I and M**exposure modes. Shoot RAW DNG for free, preview 43 film looks live, and add FilCam Pro when you want bracketing, night mode, long exposures and light trails.

[Get it on**Google Play**](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.filmode.filcam) [Coming soon on the**App Store**](https://filcam.web.app/ios/)

Android 8.0+ · free to download · no watermark · no account

ISO 1/8000 – 30" 2200 – 9500 K EV ±3 RAW + JPG

Free, and Pro

How it works

## Pick a mode, dial it in, shoot.

1

### Choose your mode

P for program, S for shutter priority, I for ISO priority, M for full manual. The mode is not a menu you dig for — it follows the dials you touch, exactly the way a camera body works.

2

### Dial it in

Drag the ruler for ISO, shutter, EV, Kelvin or focus distance, or tap a value to set it exactly. Watch focus peaking, false colour, the live histogram and the level react before you commit.

3

### Fire the shutter

Tap, press a volume key or start the self-timer. Take one frame or a burst — or, with FilCam Pro, a 3/5/7-frame bracket, a night stack or an intervalometer sequence — then edit the result without leaving the app.

Features

## The controls a camera app usually charges for.

### Full manual control

ISO, shutter speed, exposure compensation, white balance in Kelvin from 2200 to 9500 K, and manual focus distance — each on a ruler you can drag or tap. Lock AE, AWB and AF independently.

### P / S / I / M like a body

Program, shutter priority, ISO priority and full manual — the mode letter in the readout follows what you have set by hand, so you always know which half of the exposure the camera is still deciding.

### RAW DNG, free

Keep the sensor data, not the phone's guess at it. DNG files carry the real capture metadata and no baked-in look, so you can grade them in Lightroom or Darktable. RAW is free — it is not part of FilCam Pro.

### 43 film looks, live

Every look is previewed on your own scene before you press the shutter, then baked into the JPEG. Import your own .cube LUTs, add light leaks, halation, star, dust or VHS from eleven live effects, and warm or cool the frame on the colour pad.

### Peaking, false colour & scopes

Focus peaking, zebra and false colour mark the viewfinder, never the file. A live RGB histogram, parade, waveform and vectorscope, an electronic level, crop guides and ten composition grids — thirds, golden ratio, golden spiral, triangles, diagonals, centre cross, 4×4, 6×6, horizon and dynamic symmetry.

### Focus and metering you choose

AF-C, AF-S, macro, infinity or fully manual focus by distance. Matrix, centre-weighted or spot metering. Pinch to zoom, and map the volume keys to the shutter, exposure or zoom.

### Bracketing, night & interval PRO

Burst and the self-timer are free. FilCam Pro adds exposure bracketing of 3, 5 or 7 frames with your own EV step for HDR, a night mode that stacks frames, focus stacking, and an intervalometer that runs by shot count or by minutes for timelapse.

### Long exposure & light trails PRO

Waterfalls, traffic, star fields and empty night streets. The long-exposure drive runs up to 30 seconds, and light trails hold the frame open from 15 seconds to 5 minutes, keeping the brightest part of every frame while you watch it build.

### Your files, and a photo lab

Write into any folder inside Pictures, with a filename pattern built from date, time, counter, ISO and shutter, as JPEG, HEIF or PNG with full EXIF and optional geotagging. Then finish the shot in the built-in editor: curves, HSL, clarity, fade, vignette, undo and compare.

Your photos, your phone

## Your photos stay on your phone.

There is no sign-up screen, no cloud library and no sync toggle to switch off. FilCam captures, processes and writes every frame on the device, and no image ever leaves it. What does leave — anonymous usage and crash reports, so a camera that fails on your phone gets fixed — never includes a photo, a file name or a location, and Settings has one switch that stops it.

**0**photos uploaded

**0**accounts or sign-ups

**0**watermarks

Exposure modes

## Four letters, the same as on a mode dial.

You never pick the mode from a list. Set a value by hand and the camera hands you that control; leave it on auto and the camera keeps it. The letter in the readout just tells you where you stand.

P

Program

ISO and shutter both automatic. Nudge exposure compensation, frame the shot and let the meter do the arithmetic — with every other manual control still available.

S

Shutter priority

You set the shutter speed, the camera finds the ISO. Freeze a moving subject at 1/1000, or slow it down for water and motion blur.

I

ISO priority

You pin the ISO, the camera picks the shutter. Keep noise where you want it — base ISO for clean daylight frames, higher only when you choose.

M

Manual

Both halves are yours, across the whole range your sensor reports. Nothing drifts between frames, which is what makes bracketing, intervals and night work repeatable.

FAQ

## Fair questions.

**Does FilCam shoot RAW DNG?**

Yes, on phones whose camera hardware reports RAW support — most mid-range and flagship Android phones do, and the option is hidden rather than broken on the ones that do not. DNG is free and not part of FilCam Pro. You can save a DNG alongside a JPEG so you keep both the negative and a ready-to-share file, and the DNG is always the untouched sensor data with no film look baked into it.

**How long an exposure can I take?**

In S and M mode the shutter goes as long as your phone's sensor reports, free — the app reads the real limit from the camera rather than promising a number it cannot deliver. For longer, FilCam Pro adds a long-exposure drive of up to 30 seconds and light trails that stay open from 15 seconds to 5 minutes. Brace the phone or use a tripod, and trigger it with the self-timer or a volume key so you do not shake the frame.

**What is free, and what is FilCam Pro?**

Manual controls, RAW DNG, the film looks, the light effects, the viewfinder tools and the photo editor are free, with no watermark. The free version shows a small banner ad on the Settings screen only, never over the viewfinder or while you shoot, and you can watch an optional video ad to try Pro for 30 minutes. FilCam Pro removes the ads and adds the advanced drive modes — exposure bracketing, night mode, focus stacking, the intervalometer, long exposure and light trails. It is sold monthly, yearly with a 7-day free trial, or as a one-time lifetime unlock, and Google Play shows the price in your currency before you pay.

**Do my photos get uploaded anywhere?**

No. Capture, processing, LUTs and editing all run on your phone's own GPU, and no image data ever leaves the device. There is no account and no cloud library. The app does send anonymous usage and crash reports — which controls got used, and a stack trace when something fails — so that a camera that breaks on your phone gets fixed for your phone; never a photo, a file name or a location, and one switch in Settings turns it off. See the [Privacy Policy](https://trunghieuvn.github.io/filmode-camera/privacy) for the full detail.

**Where are my photos saved?**

In a folder inside your device's *Pictures* directory — *Pictures/FilCam* by default, and you can change the folder name in Settings. Files are registered with your media library, so Gallery, Google Photos and any other app see them immediately. The filename pattern is yours too, built from `{date}`, `{time}`, a counter, `{iso}` and `{shutter}`.

**Does it add GPS coordinates to my photos?**

Only if you turn on *Save location in photos* in Settings, which is off until you do. When it is on, the coordinates are written into the photo's own EXIF on the device — nothing is sent to us or to anyone else. Turn it off and no location permission is ever requested.

**Can I use my own film looks?**

Yes. Import `.cube` LUT files and they appear in the strip under the viewfinder next to the 43 built-in looks, previewed live on the scene in front of you, so the look is baked in the moment you press the shutter. The built-in editor can also save a grade back out as a `.cube` file.

**Which Android versions and languages does it support?**

Android 8.0 and newer. Some controls depend on what your camera hardware exposes — the available ISO and shutter range, HEIF encoding and RAW support all come from the device — so the app shows what your phone can actually do instead of a dead menu item. The app is in nine languages: English, Vietnamese, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi, French and Indonesian, and you can switch in Settings.

**Where do I get it?**

On [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.filmode.filcam), free to download. Check the package name — `app.filmode.filcam` — rather than the app name: a camera app's name is easy to copy, a package name is not.

Out now

## Ready when you are.

FilCam is on Google Play, free to download, with FilCam Pro there when you need it. Install it, and write to us if you want to tell us what a manual camera app still gets wrong — the phone in your hand may be one we have not tested on.

[Get it on**Google Play**](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=app.filmode.filcam) [Coming soon on the**App Store**](https://filcam.web.app/ios/)

Questions? [Support](https://trunghieuvn.github.io/filmode-camera/support) · [trunghieu4121993@gmail.com](mailto:trunghieu4121993@gmail.com)

# Privacy Policy — Groundglass for Android

> Groundglass privacy policy: what each permission is for, why photos and geotags stay on device, and the anonymous reports you can switch off.

Source: https://trunghieuvn.github.io/groundglass/privacy.html

Groundglass has moved to [trunghieuvn.github.io/groundglass](https://trunghieuvn.github.io/groundglass/). This policy is also published there, at [/privacy.html](https://trunghieuvn.github.io/groundglass/privacy), and the two copies say the same thing.

# Privacy Policy

Effective date: October 31, 2026

Groundglass — published on Google Play as *Groundglass Manual Cam Pro RAW*, package `vn.fighttech.groundglass` — is a manual camera app for Android published by FightTech VN. In short: **your photos are captured, processed and stored on your phone, they are never uploaded, and there is no account.**The app uses the internet for three things only: downloading film looks from the Presets Store when you open it, sending anonymous usage counts and crash reports, and sending anonymous daily counts of which film looks were used to our own server; one switch in Settings turns off both the reports and the look counts. There are no ads and we do not sell any data.

## What the app does

The app operates your phone's camera and writes the resulting image file to your own storage. Everything — exposure, focus, white balance, RAW conversion and the film looks — runs on your device's own CPU and GPU. There is no cloud processing, no user account and no sign-in. Nothing the app sends over the internet contains your photos or anything taken from them. It also talks to Google Play on your own phone, to show Pro prices, run a purchase you start, and check which purchases you own.

## Permissions the app declares

These are the only permissions in the app's manifest. Android asks you for the runtime ones (camera, location) at the moment each is first needed, and you can revoke them later in *Settings → Apps → Groundglass → Permissions*.

- **Camera**(`CAMERA`) — required. It is what runs the viewfinder and takes the photo. Without it the app cannot function. The camera feed is rendered on screen and written to the file you capture; it is never streamed anywhere.
- **Location, optional**(`ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION`) — used for one purpose only: writing GPS coordinates into the EXIF metadata of the photos you take, on the device. It is requested only if you switch on *Save location in photos* in the app's settings, which is off by default. The coordinates are stored inside your own image files and are not transmitted to us or to any third party. Leave the setting off and the app never asks for the permission and never reads your location. GPS hardware is declared as optional, so the app installs on phones without it.
- **Internet**(`INTERNET`, `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`) — used for the Presets Store, for anonymous usage and crash reports, and for the anonymous daily look counts, all described below. None of these is a runtime permission.
- **Google Play billing**(`com.android.vending.BILLING`) — added by Google's Play Billing library for the optional Groundglass Pro purchase. It lets the app hand a purchase to the Google Play app on your phone.
- **Background upload and install source**(`WAKE_LOCK`, `com.google.android.finsky.permission.BIND_GET_INSTALL_REFERRER_SERVICE`) — added by the Firebase SDKs. The first lets a usage or crash report that is already queued finish sending if the screen turns off; the second lets the analytics SDK read, once, which Google Play listing the app was installed from, used only for aggregate install counts and never for advertising. Neither is a runtime permission, and both stop being used when you switch the reports off.
- **Storage, on older Android only**(`WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, declared with `maxSdkVersion="28"`) — needed on Android 9 and earlier to save your photos into the shared Pictures library. On Android 10 and newer the app writes through the system MediaStore and this permission is neither declared nor requested. The app does not ask for broad access to read your existing photo library.

The app declares no contacts, microphone, phone, calendar, SMS or background-location permission, and no "all files access". It also declares **no advertising permission**: `AD_ID` and the Android Ad Services permissions are explicitly removed from the build, and advertising-ID collection is switched off in the analytics SDK, so the app cannot read your advertising identifier.

## Your photos and where they go

Photos are written into a folder inside your device's public `Pictures` directory — `Pictures/Groundglass` by default, or whichever folder name you set — and registered with your media library so Gallery and other apps can see them. You choose the file format (JPEG, plus RAW DNG on devices whose sensor supports it), the quality and the filename pattern. Photos you take belong to you and stay on your device until you move or delete them; uninstalling the app does not delete them.

The image files carry standard EXIF metadata written by the app — exposure time, ISO, aperture, focal length, white balance, orientation, the date and time from your device, and GPS coordinates if and only if you enabled geotagging. That metadata travels inside the file, so bear it in mind before sharing a photo publicly. It is written locally; we never see it.

## The Presets Store

When you open the Presets Store, the app downloads the store's catalogue and the before/after sample pictures, and, when you pick a look, that look's colour file. They come from our content server, which is delivered through Cloudflare's network. These are plain file downloads: like any web request they reveal your IP address and a standard app user-agent to that server, and they carry no account, no device identifier and nothing from your photos. If you preview a look on your own photos, the preview is rendered on your phone; the photo is never uploaded. Looks you download are kept on your phone. If you never open the store, the app never contacts it.

## Analytics and crash reporting

The app uses **Google Analytics for Firebase**and **Firebase Crashlytics**, both provided by Google, to learn which features get used and to fix crashes. Both are on by default and both stop when you switch off *Settings → Storage & privacy → Send usage and crash reports*; the choice is remembered across launches. The same switch also stops the look counts.

- **Usage counts**— which screens and camera settings are used (for example that a drive mode was chosen, that a photo was saved or shared and whether it worked, or that the paywall was opened and a purchase started, was pending, finished, failed or was cancelled, with the product ID; and whether Pro is active), the app version, the phone model, Android version, language and country, and a random app-instance ID that Firebase creates on install. Country is derived by Google from the connection; Google Analytics does not log or store IP addresses.
- **Crash reports**— when the app fails, or hits an error it recovers from (the camera failing to open, a photo that could not be saved, a LUT that could not be loaded), the stack trace and the part of the app where it happened, the phone model, Android version, free memory and disk space, orientation, a random Crashlytics installation ID, and the list of app events that led up to it.

**What is never sent:**your photographs or any part of one, thumbnails, file names, folder names, your GPS location or geotags, the contents of your media library, your advertising identifier, your name, email or any account identifier.

This data is processed by Google on our behalf, under the [Firebase privacy and security terms](https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy). It is used only to improve the app, never for advertising, never combined with other data to identify you, and never sold.

**No advertising.**The app contains no ads and no ad SDK.

## Favourites and look popularity counts

You can pin looks to the front of the camera's look strip, and star looks in the Presets Store to keep them under *Favourites*. These lists are kept in the app's private storage on your phone and are never sent anywhere.

So that we can tell which film looks people actually use, the app also keeps an anonymous count for each day: which built-in looks and which Presets Store looks you applied that day, and which you pinned, starred, unpinned or unstarred. Each look is noted at most once a day, however often you use it. LUTs you imported yourself are never recorded.

Once a day is over, the app sends it in one HTTPS POST to our own server, `https://fighttech.vn/api/v1/looks/usage` (FightTech VN). If the phone is offline it tries again later, and several finished days may then travel in the same request, each with its own token; a day still unsent after 7 days is deleted from the phone. The request holds only:

- the app's package name (`vn.fighttech.groundglass`) and the date;
- a random token drawn fresh for that one day, used only to refuse the same day if it is sent twice. The server stores only a hash of it and deletes that after 9 days;
- for each look, its built-in ID (for example `vint-neg-1`) and whether you applied, starred (or pinned) or unstarred it that day.

It holds **no**installation ID, advertising ID, account, device model, photo, file name or location, so two days cannot be linked to each other or to your phone. The server keeps only totals: for each app, day and look, how many installs used it, starred it and unstarred it, and how many installs reported that day. The totals are kept for 400 days, then deleted. This endpoint stores nothing about the request itself: not your IP address, which, like any web request, the network and the server see while it is handled, and not the standard header Android adds to web requests, which names the Android version and phone model. The totals are visible only to FightTech VN, in an internal report that hides any look used by fewer than 5 installs. They are never sold or shared.

The counts stop when you switch off *Settings → Storage & privacy → Send usage and crash reports*, the same switch as the analytics. Switching it off also deletes the days not yet sent.

## Data we collect

**Only the anonymous usage counts and crash reports described above**, which we see as totals and individual crash reports in the Firebase console, **and the anonymous daily look totals**on our own server. We — FightTech VN — hold no database of users, and we never see your photos or your settings. There is no account system and no newsletter.

**Purchases.**Groundglass Pro (bracket, night, long exposure, focus stacking, interval and light-trail modes, and the Presets Store's Pro looks) is sold as a monthly or yearly subscription or a one-time lifetime unlock through Google Play Billing. Google processes the payment under the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy); your card details and billing address are never given to us or to the app. As the seller, Google Play Console shows us the order record for each purchase — order ID, product, date, price and country — which we use only for refunds, tax and support, and not to identify or contact you. The app verifies the purchase on your phone with Google's signature and remembers the result locally; it sends nothing about it to us. The built-in film looks, RAW and every manual control are free and need no purchase.

## Data shared with third parties

**None is sold or shared for advertising.**Google receives the usage counts and crash reports as the service provider that runs Firebase for us, and Cloudflare delivers the Presets Store's files; neither receives your photos. The daily look counts go to our own server, not to a third party. Google Play runs any Groundglass Pro purchase itself, as described above.

## Data retention and deletion

Your settings, saved preferences and downloaded looks live on your device and are removed when you uninstall the app. Photos you have taken are yours and stay in `Pictures` until you delete them.

Firebase Crashlytics keeps crash reports for 90 days. Google Analytics keeps user-level event data for the retention period set in our project, at most 14 months, after which only aggregated totals remain. On our server, the anonymous per-day look totals are kept for 400 days, then deleted; days not yet sent stay on the phone for at most 7 days. Switching off *Send usage and crash reports* stops any new data, including the look counts, and deletes the days of look counts not yet sent; clearing the app's data or reinstalling it creates a new random app-instance ID, so earlier data can no longer be linked to your phone. Look counts already sent are anonymous totals that cannot be traced back to you, so they cannot be deleted for one person. You can also write to us at the address below. You can cancel a subscription or request a refund in the Google Play app under *Payments & subscriptions*.

## Children

The app is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect personal information from children.

## Your responsibility

You are responsible for the photographs you take and how you use them, including consent of the people you photograph and the law of the place you are shooting in.

## Changes to this policy

If the app's data practices change, this page will be updated and the date above revised before the new version is released. If a future version adds a permission or an SDK, it will be listed here first. *Written on September 5, 2026 for the first Groundglass release, which shipped with no analytics, no crash reporting and no internet permission. Revised on September 21, 2026 for the release that added the optional Groundglass Pro purchase through Google Play Billing. Revised on September 27, 2026 for the release that adds the internet permission, for the Presets Store and for anonymous usage and crash reports through Firebase, with the switch in Settings that turns the reports off. Revised on October 31, 2026 for the release that adds favourites and the anonymous daily look counts sent to our own server, which the same switch turns off.*

## Contact

Questions about this policy, or a request about your data? Email [trunghieu4121993@gmail.com](mailto:trunghieu4121993@gmail.com).

# Privacy Policy — FilCam for Android

> FilCam privacy policy: what each permission is for, why photos and geotags stay on your device, and what the free version's ads and usage reports send.

Source: https://trunghieuvn.github.io/filmode-camera/privacy.html

# Privacy Policy

Effective date: November 3, 2026

FilCam — published on Google Play as *FilCam: Pro Manual RAW Camera*, package `app.filmode.filcam` — is a manual camera app for Android published by FightTech. This policy describes exactly what the app accesses on your device and what leaves it. In short: **your photos are captured, processed and stored on your phone, they are never uploaded, and there is no account.**The app uses the internet for four things only: downloading film looks from the Presets Store when you open it, sending anonymous usage and crash reports, so that a camera that fails on your phone can be fixed for your phone, sending anonymous daily counts of which film looks were used to our own server, and, in the free version, showing ads from Google AdMob — a banner on the Settings screen only, and a rewarded video you can choose to watch for 30 minutes of Pro — which use your device's advertising ID subject to the consent choices you make. FilCam Pro removes all ads. The sections below list exactly what each involves, and one switch in Settings turns the reports and the look counts off. We do not sell any data.

## What the app does

The app operates your phone's camera, applies the settings and film look you choose, and writes the resulting image file to your own storage. Everything — exposure, colour, LUTs, RAW conversion and the built-in photo editor — runs on your device's own CPU and GPU. There is no cloud processing of your images, no user account and no sign-in. Nothing the app sends over the internet contains your photos or anything taken from them: its only network traffic is the Presets Store downloads, the anonymous usage and crash reporting, the anonymous daily look counts and, in the free version, the ads and their settings, all described below. It also talks to Google Play on your own phone, to show FilCam Pro prices, run a purchase you start, and check which purchases you own.

## Permissions the app declares

These are the only permissions in the app's manifest, including the ones Google's ad library adds to it. Android asks you for the runtime ones (camera, microphone, location) at the moment each is first needed, and you can revoke any of those later in *Settings → Apps → FilCam → Permissions*; the network and billing permissions are granted at install time.

- **Camera**(`CAMERA`) — required. It is what runs the viewfinder and takes the photo. Without it the app cannot function. The camera feed is rendered on screen and written to the file you capture; it is never streamed anywhere.
- **Location, optional**(`ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`, `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION`) — used for one purpose only: writing GPS coordinates into the EXIF metadata of the photos you take, on the device. It is requested only if you switch on *Save location in photos* in the app's settings, which is off by default. The coordinates are stored inside your own image files and are not transmitted to us or to any third party. Leave the setting off and the app never asks for the permission and never reads your location. GPS hardware is declared as optional, so the app installs on phones without it.
- **Microphone, optional**(`RECORD_AUDIO`) — used for one purpose only: recording sound into the videos you shoot with the Pro camera. It is requested the first time a clip records with *Record sound* on; turn that setting off, or deny the permission, and clips are recorded silent. The sound is written into your own video file on the device and is never transmitted to us or to anyone else. The microphone is declared as optional hardware.
- **Storage, on older Android only**(`WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, declared with `maxSdkVersion="28"`) — needed on Android 9 and earlier to save your photos into the shared Pictures library. On Android 10 and newer the app writes through the system MediaStore and this permission is neither declared nor requested. The app does not ask for broad access to read your existing photo library.
- **Network**(`INTERNET`, `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE`, `WAKE_LOCK`) — these are not permissions Android asks you about; they are granted at install time. They are used for four things: downloading the Presets Store's catalogue and looks when you open the store, delivering a usage or crash report (the wake lock lets a report that is already queued finish sending if the screen turns off), sending the anonymous daily look counts to our server, and, in the free version, loading ads and the ad settings described under Advertising. The reporting libraries add one Play Store permission, `com.google.android.finsky.permission.BIND_GET_INSTALL_REFERRER_SERVICE`, which lets Google Play tell the app which listing the install came from. Nothing else in the app uses the network, and nothing you shot is ever uploaded.
- **Advertising ID and Android ad services**(`com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID`, `ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID`, `ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION`, `ACCESS_ADSERVICES_TOPICS`) — added by Google's AdMob library for the ads in the free version. They let the ad SDKs read your device's resettable advertising identifier and use Android's own ad-measurement features, as described under Advertising. Firebase Analytics keeps advertising-ID collection switched off, so only the ad SDKs read it. None is a runtime permission. You can reset or delete this ID in Android's own settings (*Settings → Privacy → Ads*, or *Google → Ads* on some phones).
- **Google Play billing**(`com.android.vending.BILLING`) — added by Google's Play Billing library for the optional FilCam Pro purchase. It lets the app hand a purchase to the Google Play app on your phone.

The app declares no contacts, phone, calendar, SMS or background-location permission, and no "all files access". Apart from GPS geotags you switch on yourself, the only location data is the **approximate location**(a coarse region estimated from your IP address) that the ad SDKs collect in the free version, described under Advertising.

## Your photos and where they go

Photos are written into a folder inside your device's public `Pictures` directory — `Pictures/Filmode` by default, or whichever folder name you set — and registered with your media library so Gallery and other apps can see them. You choose the file format (JPEG, HEIF or PNG, plus RAW DNG on devices that support it), the quality and the filename pattern. Photos you take belong to you and stay on your device until you move or delete them; uninstalling the app does not delete them.

The image files carry standard EXIF metadata written by the app — exposure time, ISO, aperture, focal length, white balance, orientation, the date and time from your device, and GPS coordinates if and only if you enabled geotagging. That metadata travels inside the file, so bear it in mind before sharing a photo publicly. It is written locally; we never see it.

## The Presets Store

When you open the Presets Store, the app downloads the store's catalogue (`filmode.app/store/manifest.json` and `filmode.app/store/trending.json`) and the before/after sample pictures, and, when you pick a look, that look's colour file. They come from our content server at `filmode.app`, which is delivered through Cloudflare's network. These are plain file downloads: like any web request they reveal your IP address and a standard app user-agent to that server, and they carry no account, no device identifier and nothing from your photos. Looks you download are kept on your phone. If you never open the store, the app never contacts it.

*Match my photos* picks looks that suit your own pictures — the last few stills FilCam took, or photos you choose in Android's photo picker. The matching and every preview are computed on your phone; no photo, thumbnail or colour data from a photo is uploaded.

## Advertising

The free version of FilCam shows ads from **Google AdMob**: a **banner on the Settings screen only**, never on the camera screen, and an optional **rewarded video ad**that you choose to watch from the FilCam Pro screen to unlock every Pro feature for 30 minutes (ads stay on during those 30 minutes). Full-screen interstitial and app-open ads are built into the app but are currently switched off from our server. The **Unity Ads**SDK is bundled as a fallback network for when AdMob has no ad to show, and is also switched off from our server. Which ad formats and networks are on can be changed remotely without an app update, but ads never appear over the viewfinder or during recording.

**FilCam Pro removes all ads.**Once you have Pro (a purchase or a subscription), no ad is shown and the ad SDKs are not started.

To know which ad formats are on, the free version asks our own server, `https://fighttech.vn/api/v1/flags` (FightTech), when it starts. The request carries only the app's package name (`app.filmode.filcam`) — no identifier and nothing from your photos — and the answer, a set of on/off switches, is kept on the phone for the next launch.

To serve and measure ads, these SDKs may collect: your device's **advertising ID**, IP address (used to estimate an approximate location), device model, Android version, language, app version, your interactions with ads and the app (an ad was shown, clicked, watched to the end, or failed to load), and diagnostics about how the ad SDK runs. They use this to show ads, cap how often you see them, prevent fraud and measure performance, and share it with advertisers and ad partners for those purposes.

- **Personalised ads**use your advertising ID and interests inferred by the ad network across apps.
- **Non-personalised ads**are chosen from context only (the app, a coarse location, the time) and are not based on your past behaviour. Ad networks still use limited data for frequency capping, fraud prevention and aggregate reporting.

Which one you get depends on your consent choices and on the law where you are. How Google and Unity handle this data: [Google's use of data from partner apps](https://policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites), [Unity's privacy policy](https://unity.com/legal/game-player-and-app-user-privacy-policy).

## Consent and privacy options

FilCam uses the **Google User Messaging Platform (UMP)**, a certified consent tool. Where the law requires it (for example in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and some US states), a consent form appears before any ad is requested. You can accept, refuse, or choose purposes and partners one by one. If you refuse, you still get non-personalised (or limited) ads, and the app works the same.

**To change your choice later:**open *Settings → Privacy options (ads)* in the app. The row appears whenever the consent form applies to you; it reopens the form so you can change or withdraw consent at any time. Your choice is stored on the phone by the UMP SDK and passed to the ad networks with each ad request.

You can also reset or delete your advertising ID in Android's settings, which cuts the link to previous ad data. The *Send usage and crash reports* switch controls our analytics, not the ads.

## Analytics and crash reporting

From version 1.0.1 FilCam includes two Google libraries: **Firebase Analytics**(Google Analytics for Firebase) and **Firebase Crashlytics**. They exist for one reason. Manual camera control on Android depends on what each manufacturer exposes through the Camera2 API, and it differs from phone to phone; without a crash report we cannot know that RAW capture fails on some particular model, and cannot fix it.

**What is sent.**

- **Which features you used**, as plain counters with no content — that a photo was captured, saved or shared, that a LUT or a preset was applied or imported, that a recipe was saved, that a long exposure was taken, and which of the two screens (camera, photo editor) you were on; in the Presets Store, that it was opened, which look or pack was viewed or used, and how many looks were matched to your photos; and on the FilCam Pro screen, that it was opened, which plan was selected, whether a purchase started, was pending, was cancelled or failed (with the plan's product ID), and whether Pro is active on the phone or was just gained or lost; in the free version, ad counters — that the ad SDKs started, an ad loaded, was shown, tapped, closed, went stale or failed to load (with its format, network, placement and error code), what AdMob reports a shown ad earned, that a rewarded ad was watched to the end and the 30-minute Pro pass opened, and that your personalised-ads answer changed. Never the photo, never the file, never the name of the LUT file you imported.
- **Crash and error reports**— the stack trace when the app crashes, or when an operation fails and the app recovers (opening the camera, taking a picture, writing a DNG, saving or exporting a photo, loading a LUT), the name of the operation that failed, and the recent in-app steps that led up to it. Reports are attributed to the app with an `app` key so we can tell FilCam's reports from our other apps'.
- **Device and app context**collected automatically by those libraries: your phone's model and manufacturer, the Android version, the app version, the language and country setting, the screen size, and a randomly generated installation identifier that Google's SDK creates. That identifier is not your advertising ID — advertising-ID collection is switched off in Firebase Analytics (`google_analytics_adid_collection_enabled` is `false`), and only the ad SDKs read it, as described under Advertising — and it is reset if you clear the app's data or reinstall.

**What is never sent:**your photographs or any part of one, thumbnails, file names, folder names, your GPS location or geotags, the location or contents of your imported LUT files, the contents of your media library, your advertising identifier, your name, your email or any account identifier. There is no account, so there is nothing to attach a report to a person by.

**The switch.**Open *Settings* in the app and turn off *Send usage and crash reports*. It is on when you install the app; switching it off stops collection in both libraries immediately, for as long as it stays off, and no further report leaves the device. The same switch also stops the look counts. Uninstalling the app has the same effect.

**Who processes it.**Google, as our processor, under the [Firebase privacy documentation](https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy) and [Google's Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy). The data lands in our Firebase project and is visible only to us, in aggregate; we do not attempt to identify anyone from it, and we do not sell it, share it or use it for ad targeting. Retention follows Firebase's own settings: user-level analytics data is kept for 2 months, Google's default, which we have not extended, and Crashlytics reports are kept for 90 days.

**Advertising.**The usage and crash reports never carry your advertising ID and are not used for ad targeting. The ads in the free version are a separate matter, run by the ad SDKs and described under Advertising; this switch does not turn them off.

## Favourites and look popularity counts

You can pin looks to the front of the camera's look strip, star looks in the photo editor, and star looks in the Presets Store to keep them under *Favourites*. These lists are kept in the app's private storage on your phone and are never sent anywhere.

So that we can tell which film looks people actually use, the app also keeps an anonymous count for each day: which built-in looks and which Presets Store looks you applied that day, in the camera or the editor, and which you pinned, starred, unpinned or unstarred. Each look is noted at most once a day, however often you use it. LUTs you imported and looks you saved yourself are never recorded.

Once a day is over, the app sends it in one HTTPS POST to our own server, `https://fighttech.vn/api/v1/looks/usage` (FightTech). If the phone is offline it tries again later, and several finished days may then travel in the same request, each with its own token; a day still unsent after 7 days is deleted from the phone. The request holds only:

- the app's package name (`app.filmode.filcam`) and the date;
- a random token drawn fresh for that one day, used only to refuse the same day if it is sent twice. The server stores only a hash of it and deletes that after 9 days;
- for each look, its built-in ID (for example `vint-neg-1`) and whether you applied, starred (or pinned) or unstarred it that day.

It holds **no**installation identifier, advertising identifier, account, device model, photo, file name or location, so two days cannot be linked to each other or to your phone. The server keeps only totals: for each app, day and look, how many installs used it, starred it and unstarred it, and how many installs reported that day. The totals are kept for 400 days, then deleted. This endpoint stores nothing about the request itself: not your IP address, which, like any web request, the network and the server see while it is handled, and not the standard header Android adds to web requests, which names the Android version and phone model. The totals are visible only to us, in an internal report that hides any look used by fewer than 5 installs. They are never sold or shared.

The counts stop when you switch off *Settings → Send usage and crash reports*, the same switch as the reports above. Switching it off also deletes the days not yet sent.

## Data we collect

We — FightTech — hold no database of this app's users. What reaches us is only the anonymous usage and crash reporting described above, through Google's Firebase, and the anonymous daily look totals on our own server, and only while you leave that switch on. **We never see your photos, your files or your location.**The ad data described under Advertising goes to Google (and to Unity, if it is switched on), not to us; we see only aggregate ad reports. There is no account system and no newsletter.

**Purchases.**FilCam Pro (HDR bracketing, handheld night, long exposure, focus stacking, interval and light-trail modes, and the Presets Store's trending looks and Signature pack) is sold as a monthly or yearly subscription or a one-time lifetime unlock through Google Play Billing. Google processes the payment under the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy); your card details and billing address are never given to us or to the app. As the seller, Google Play Console shows us the order record for each purchase — order ID, product, date, price and country — which we use only for refunds, tax and support, and not to identify or contact you. The app checks the purchase on your phone with Google's signature and remembers the result locally; it sends nothing about it to us. RAW, every manual control, the built-in looks and the free store packs need no purchase.

## Data shared with third parties

No data is sold. **Google AdMob and the User Messaging Platform**serve the free version's ads and ask for consent, and share the ad data described under Advertising with advertisers and ad partners. **Unity Technologies**' Unity Ads SDK is bundled as a fallback ad network but switched off by default. **Google's Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics**receive the usage counts and crash reports as our processor for the reporting described above. **Cloudflare**delivers the Presets Store's files and so sees the download requests described above. The daily look counts and the ad settings request go to our own server, not to a third party. **Google Play**runs any FilCam Pro purchase itself, as described above. None of them receives your photos.

## Data retention and deletion

All app data — your settings, imported LUTs, saved presets and recipes — lives on your device and is removed when you uninstall the app. Photos you have taken are yours and stay in `Pictures` until you delete them.

Usage reports are kept for 2 months and crash reports for 90 days, then deleted by Google automatically. Days of look counts not yet sent stay on the phone for at most 7 days; on our server, the anonymous per-day look totals are kept for 400 days, then deleted. AdMob and Unity keep ad data under their own retention policies, linked under Advertising; resetting your advertising ID breaks the link to past ad data. Nothing else about you is retained anywhere: we hold no account, profile or user database for FilCam.

### How to request deletion of your FilCam data

1. **Stop new reports.**Open FilCam, go to *Settings → Send usage and crash reports* and switch it off. From that moment the app sends no reports and no look counts, and the days of look counts not yet sent are deleted.
2. **Clear what is on your phone.**Uninstalling FilCam — or *Settings → Apps → FilCam → Storage → Clear data* — removes every setting, preset and LUT the app has stored, and resets its random installation identifier, so any later report cannot be linked to an earlier one. Your photographs are not touched: they stay in `Pictures` until you delete them yourself.
3. **Ask us to delete reports already sent.**Email [trunghieu4121993@gmail.com](mailto:trunghieu4121993@gmail.com?subject=FilCam%20data%20deletion%20request) with the subject *FilCam data deletion request*. Tell us your phone model and roughly when you used the app; we hold no name, email or account that could otherwise point us to you. We reply within 30 days and have the matching Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics records deleted.

**What gets deleted:**the anonymous usage counters, crash and error reports, the device and app context sent with them, and the app's random installation identifier. **What is kept:**nothing about you — and, on your own phone, your photographs, which are yours and which we never receive. Anything not deleted on request expires by itself on the schedule above: 2 months for usage data, 90 days for crash reports. **Look counts already sent**are anonymous totals that cannot be traced back to you, so they cannot be deleted for one person; they expire after 400 days.

## Children

The app is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect personal information from children.

## Your responsibility

You are responsible for the photographs you take and how you use them, including consent of the people you photograph and the law of the place you are shooting in.

## Changes to this policy

If the app's data practices change, this page will be updated and the date above revised before the new version is released. If a future version adds a permission or an SDK, it will be listed here first. *Revised on September 6, 2026 for version 1.0.1, which adds Firebase Analytics and Crashlytics, the network permissions they need, and the *Send usage and crash reports* switch that turns them off. Version 1.0.0 had none of these and no network access at all. Revised on September 28, 2026 for version 1.0.22, which adds the Presets Store and its downloads, and to list the optional microphone for Pro video and the FilCam Pro purchase through Google Play Billing. Revised on October 31, 2026 for the release that adds favourites and the anonymous daily look counts sent to our own server, which the same switch turns off. Updated on November 3, 2026 to add ads.*

Questions about this policy, or a request about your data? Email [trunghieu4121993@gmail.com](mailto:trunghieu4121993@gmail.com).

# Support & Help — FilCam for Android

> FilCam help: the P/S/I/M modes, long exposures and RAW DNG, bracketing and the intervalometer, where photos are saved, and how to reach us.

Source: https://trunghieuvn.github.io/filmode-camera/support.html

# FilCam Support

Everything below applies to the Android app, package `app.filmode.filcam`.

## Contact us

Email [trunghieu4121993@gmail.com](mailto:trunghieu4121993@gmail.com). We usually answer within two business days. Please include your phone model, your Android version, and — for anything about a specific photo — the mode, ISO, shutter and format you were shooting with.

## Getting started

- Grant the camera permission when the app first asks. Nothing works without it.
- Tap **PRO**to open the manual panel. Pick a channel — ISO, SHUTTER, EV, WB or FOCUS — and drag its ruler, or tap a value to jump straight to it.
- A channel you have not touched stays on **AUTO**. Tap **RESET**on a channel to hand it back to the camera.
- Press the shutter, or a volume key if you have mapped it. The frame you just took is one tap away from the editor.

## How the P / S / I / M modes work

There is no mode dial to hunt for — the letter in the readout is derived from what you have set by hand. Everything automatic is **P**. Set the shutter yourself and you are in **S**. Set the ISO yourself and you are in **I**. Set both and you are in **M**. Reset a channel and the letter moves back on its own.

## Shooting a long exposure

Open the SHUTTER channel and drag it towards the long end — up to 30 seconds, or your sensor's own maximum if that is shorter. Put the phone on something solid, use the self-timer (3 or 10 seconds) or a volume key so your finger does not move the frame, and expect the capture to take at least as long as the exposure you set. In **M**mode nothing drifts between frames, which is what you want for light trails and night work.

## RAW DNG

Switch the format to DNG in Settings. DNG holds the raw sensor data with the real capture metadata and *no* film look baked in — that is the point of it — so if you also want a ready-to-share picture, save JPEG alongside. RAW depends on your camera hardware reporting support for it; on a phone that does not, the option is not offered rather than failing silently. Open the files in Lightroom, Darktable, RawTherapee or Apple Photos.

## Bracketing, burst and the intervalometer

- **Bracket**— choose 3, 5 or 7 frames, the EV step between them, and a shift if you want the series centred somewhere other than the metered exposure. Merge them later in your HDR tool of choice.
- **Burst**— set how many frames to take and hold the shutter.
- **Interval**— set the gap between shots and either a number of shots or a duration in minutes. It can bracket each interval too. Keep the phone plugged in and cool for a long run; a hot phone will throttle.
- **Self-timer**— off, 3 or 10 seconds, and it works with every drive mode.

## Focus and metering

Focus modes are AF-C (continuous), AF-S (single), Macro, Infinity and MF. In MF the ruler sets an actual focus distance, which is what you want for a locked-off timelapse or a night scene the autofocus cannot find. Metering is Matrix, Centre-weighted or Spot, and AE-L, AWB-L and AF-L lock exposure, white balance and focus independently so a series stays consistent.

## Framing aids

The viewfinder can show a live RGB histogram, an electronic level, a crop guide and a composition grid — thirds, golden ratio, golden spiral, golden triangles, diagonals, centre cross, 4×4, 6×6, horizon or dynamic symmetry. Turn each on in Settings, along with the DSLR-style readout and the full-screen viewfinder.

## Where are my photos?

In `Pictures/Filmode` on your internal storage by default; change the folder name in **Settings → Folder inside Pictures**. Files are registered with your media library, so Gallery, Google Photos and every other app see them right away. The filename pattern is yours to set, built from `{date}`, `{time}`, `{n}`, `{iso}`, `{shutter}` and `{app}`.

## File formats and quality

JPEG, HEIF and PNG, at Maximum, Fine or Normal quality — plus RAW DNG where the hardware allows. HEIF is offered only on devices whose encoder supports it. Every file gets full EXIF: exposure time, ISO, focal length, white balance, orientation and date.

## Geotagging

Off by default. Turn on **Settings → Save location in photos**and the app asks for the location permission, then writes GPS coordinates into each photo's EXIF on the device. Nothing is sent anywhere. If you see "Location permission not granted", grant it in *Settings → Apps → FilCam → Permissions* or switch geotagging back off.

## Film looks and the photo editor

The strip under the viewfinder previews each look on your live scene, and the look is baked in the moment you press the shutter. Import your own `.cube` LUT files to add to it. After the shot, the editor gives you exposure, contrast, clarity, highlights, shadows, temperature, saturation, fade, vignette, sharpen, blur, an 8-band HSL panel, a five-point tone curve and a white-balance eyedropper — with undo, hold-to-compare, and the option to save a grade as your own LUT or recipe.

## Something is missing or greyed out

- Camera capability differs by phone. The ISO and shutter ranges, the longest exposure, HEIF encoding and RAW support are all read from your hardware — if your device does not report a capability, the app hides the control rather than offering a dead button.
- The front camera usually offers a much narrower manual range than the rear one.
- If a capture fails, check free storage first: RAW and PNG files are large.
- Still stuck? Email us with the phone model, Android version and what you were trying to shoot.

## Requesting a feature or reporting a bug

Write to us with what you expected and what happened instead. Screenshots help, and so does the EXIF of a photo that came out wrong. Feature requests are genuinely welcome — this app is being built now, and what people ask for shapes what gets built next.

# Terms of Use

Effective date: November 3, 2026

These terms govern your use of FilCam — published on Google Play as *FilCam: Pro Manual RAW Camera*, package `app.filmode.filcam` — published by FightTech. By installing or using the app you agree to them.

## 1. What the app is

The app is a camera. It operates the camera hardware in your Android device, exposes manual controls over it, writes the resulting photographs to your own storage, and lets you edit them afterwards. It does not host, provide, stream or download any content, and it does not connect to a server of ours.

## 2. Licence

We grant you a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use the app free of charge on Android devices you own or control, for as long as you comply with these terms and with the Google Play Terms of Service. You may not reverse-engineer, decompile or redistribute the app, except where that right cannot be restricted by law.

## 3. Price

The app is free to download. FilCam Pro is optional and is sold through Google Play at the prices Google Play shows you before you buy. The free version shows ads from Google AdMob: a banner on the Settings screen only, and an optional video ad you can choose to watch to use Pro for 30 minutes. Ads never appear over the viewfinder or while you shoot, and Pro removes them; see the Privacy Policy for the data the ad SDKs use.

## 4. Your photographs

You own the photographs you take, and you are solely responsible for them: for having the right to photograph your subject, for the consent of the people in the frame where the law requires it, for the places you photograph in, and for how you use, publish or share the result. We claim no rights in your images and never receive them.

## 5. Your files

Photographs are written to your own device storage and stay there. The app does not delete or modify files it did not create. You are responsible for backing up your photographs; we cannot recover anything lost or deleted.

## 6. Location and metadata

If you enable *Save location in photos*, GPS coordinates are written into the EXIF metadata of the photographs you take. That metadata travels with the file when you share it. You are responsible for deciding whether to enable the setting and for what you subsequently share. See the [Privacy Policy](https://trunghieuvn.github.io/filmode-camera/privacy).

## 7. No warranty

The app is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind. Camera capability differs enormously between Android devices: the available ISO and shutter range, the longest exposure, HEIF encoding, RAW DNG support and the accuracy of manual focus all come from your phone's own hardware and drivers. We do not guarantee that any particular control, format or exposure time will be available on your device, nor that every photograph will be captured successfully.

## 8. Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law, FightTech is not liable for indirect or consequential damages, or for any loss of photographs, data or storage space, or for a missed shot, arising from use of the app. Nothing here limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited, and these terms do not affect the statutory consumer rights you have under Vietnamese law or the law of your country of residence.

## 9. Changes and availability

We may update the app or these terms. Material changes will be reflected here with a new effective date; continued use after an update means you accept the revised terms. We may stop distributing the app; copies already installed continue to work as-is.
